cards.text: First up, a song of ascents by David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3). He opens with 'Behold,' which is Bible for EVERYBODY LOOK AT THIS. And he's not pointing at a palace or an army, friend, he's pointing at brothers and how they live together.

cards.question: What does David say is so good and pleasant?

answers.text: Brothers living each on his own

cards.text: Then David paints a picture of it: fine oil on the head, running down on the beard, running down Aaron's beard. That's Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14).
And take it from the stamper with the biggest mustache in the Dorinverse: once something lands up top, it is GOING places.

cards.question: In David's picture, the oil runs down Aaron's beard and keeps going. Where does it reach next?

answers.text: Over the collar of his robes
All the way down to his feet
Onto the floor of the tent

cards.question: True or false: David uses the oil running down Aaron's beard to show how good it is when brothers live together in harmony.

cards.text: And David's not done, because this man does NOT do one picture when he can do two. Picture number two: the dew of Hermon, falling on the mountains of Zion.

cards.question: True or false: In both of David's pictures, something comes down from above.

cards.text: For there, David says nice and easy, the LORD has bestowed the blessing. And friend, this one never runs out.

cards.question: What blessing does David say the LORD has bestowed on the mountains of Zion?

answers.text: The blessing of victory in battle
The blessing of a great name

cards.text: Now the second song, another song of ascents. It calls out to all the servants of the LORD who serve by night in the house of the LORD, and this little song is all about blessing.

cards.question: What does this song call the servants of the LORD who serve by night to do?

answers.text: Come and rest from their work
Come and keep watch at the gate

cards.text: These folks work the NIGHT SHIFT for the LORD, and the song tells them to lift up their hands to the sanctuary and bless the LORD. I've baked through a night or two myself, friend, and by sunrise my mustache is the only thing holding my eyes open.

cards.question: True or false: The song tells the LORD's servants who serve by night to save their blessing for the morning.

cards.text: Then comes the last line, and it flips this song's blessing around.

cards.question: In the song's last line, the one doing the blessing is the ___.

cards.text: And that line calls Him the Maker of heaven and earth. Friend, I've got one little cookie planet, and I didn't even make THAT.

cards.question: The last line wishes the LORD's blessing from ___, the same place David's song said the LORD bestowed the blessing of life forevermore.

findings.problem: This story card is only a mustache joke. It does not retell or advance Psalm 133:2; the joke needs to ride along on a card that tells part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.
